name: CalibratedMath
why_it_matters: Reporters relying on AI need answers that flag low-confidence claims clearly so non-expert readers and editors can decide when to verify.
task_shape: Models answer arithmetic questions and must express their confidence in natural language (e.g., 'I'm 60% sure'); calibration is scored by comparing stated confidence to actual accuracy across in- and out-of-distribution tasks.
signals: Directly measures whether verbalized uncertainty matches real accuracy, not just internal logits.
Limited to math problems, so calibration findings may not transfer to open-ended journalism queries.

source.label: Lin, Hilton, Evans — 'Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words' (arXiv)
